# Hormuz traffic plunges as Iran prepares China talks

An Indian liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carrier, Shivalik, arrives at Mundra Port via the Strait of Hormuz, amid the US-Israel conflict with Iran, in Gujarat, India, March 16, 2026.



Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz fell sharply as Iran prepared diplomatic talks in China, while attacks on Saudi Arabia and damage to Persian Gulf cloud infrastructure underscored the widening consequences of the war on Tuesday.

Only four commodity vessels crossed Hormuz on Monday, down from 10 on Sunday, Reuters reported, citing preliminary Kpler data. Two dry-bulk carriers exited, one carrying cargo and the other empty, while two empty oil tankers entered. The figures exclude ships that may have crossed with their tracking transponders switched off. TankerTrackers separately said two-way daytime traffic by very large crude carriers was continuing.

The dangers facing shipping were illustrated by the Panama-flagged tanker Elgaia, which Oman’s Maritime Security Center said was being towed to port after catching fire following an earlier attack.

An Omani naval vessel evacuated 23 crew members and arranged medical care, while searches continued for two missing people. The incident occurred about 1.3 nautical miles northeast of Musandam governorate. The statement did not identify an attacker.

Pressure also intensified around Bab el-Mandeb, the southern gateway to the Red Sea. Commodity-vessel transits there fell to 21 on Monday from 28

Omani Foreign Minister Badr al Busaidi visited Tehran on August 25, 2026 for talks with his counterpart Abbas Araghchi.



Iranian lawmakers, hardline media and analysts have blamed Washington for postponing Oman-hosted talks on Strait of Hormuz shipping arrangements, despite officials attributing the delay to regional objections and Saudi concerns over Yemen.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said the meeting, scheduled for Monday in Salalah, was postponed “in the interests of consensus.” An Iranian Foreign Ministry official separately said the delay came at the request of “some regional countries,” while spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Saudi Arabia had sought the postponement because of developments in Yemen.

No new date has been announced for the meeting.

Baghaei described the planned gathering as an “opportunity” created by Iran and Oman and urged regional states not to let it slip away.

# Iran war has cost the US more than $38 billion, budget office says

![Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth (right) spoke during a meeting with German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius (left) at the Pentagon Tuesday.](https://bostonglobe-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/resizer/v2/52PYX64PHJENBJY2IX3DOCA7XQ.jpg?auth=7988f68978458bf93b502297e9ac63822b428831f046b4251e57bed803c437c5&width=1440)

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth (right) spoke during a meeting with German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius (left) at the Pentagon Tuesday.MANDEL NGAN/AFP via Getty Images

WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. war against Iran has cost the Department of Defense [more than $38 billion through Aug. 1](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/62756 "https://www.cbo.gov/publication/62756"), and will continue costing up to $3 billion a month or more depending on the intensity of the conflict, according to an assessment released Tuesday by the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office.

CBO said the war is expected to contribute to inflation into the first quarter of 2027, making inflation roughly 0.5 percentage points higher than they had previously estimated. That’s driven largely by the reduction of oil and natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and disruptions to shipping through the Red Sea.

China’s call for a collective BRICS role in restoring peace in the Persian Gulf and Middle East has triggered debate in Iran over whether Beijing is preparing to mediate between Tehran and Washington.

Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that Beijing was willing to work with other BRICS members to help restore peace and stability in the Persian Gulf and the Middle East, offering a four-point proposal aimed at reducing tensions, ending hostilities and promoting peace.

Xi’s remarks at the opening of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi marked China’s first public signal since the Iran-US war began six months ago that it was willing to take an active role in addressing the crisis through a coordinated BRICS effort.

events.summary: Xi’s BRICS peace call sparks debate in Iran over China’s role in war

# US military destroyed Iranian boats after attempt to seize Navy drone - Axios

The US military destroyed two Iranian small boats on Monday after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps tried to seize a US Navy unmanned vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, Axios reported, citing US officials.

A US official told Axios that an American drone fired two missiles at the boats after US forces identified the attempt to take control of the naval drone.

"Iranian small boats recently attempted to take possession of a US unmanned surface vessel, but they were unsuccessful after CENTCOM forcefully responded," US Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins told Axios.

"The surface drone remains under US operational control," Hawkins said.

Iranian media had earlier reported that two fishing boats were struck near Kargan and Larak Island in Hormozgan province. A provincial official said some fishermen were missing and search-and-rescue operations were underway.

The incident came as the United States sought to increase protected commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, Axios said.
